title: When the Garden Sings Anew
premise: Lior Okonkwo, youngest and least gifted member of the Verdant Guild, has spent their whole life in a valley where magic cannot follow — until a feral child arrives speaking the First Tongue, the language that once commanded living things. The child is the last uncorrupted piece of King Aldric, whose crown has been slowly devouring him and whose kingdom's magic now bleeds toward the valley, threatening to break the ward that keeps it dead. Lior must escort the child through a land where every song, tree, and oath remembers the old magic, learning that they themselves were born inside the valley because they are woven from its last thread of wild power. In the end Lior chooses truth over loyalty to the guild that raised them: they sing the child's language back into the king, unbinding him at the cost of their own place in the valley, and step into a world where belonging must be built rather than inherited.
about_author: O. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former botanist who left fieldwork to write about places where the natural world refuses to stay quiet. They live at the edge of an old forest and insist the birds there know more than they let on.

chapters.title: The Door That Should Not Knock
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On the eve of the guild's centennial rite, a mud-caked child appears at the valley gate speaking words no one understands — except the ancient garden, which blooms out of season in answer. Lior, dismissed by the elders as talentless, alone notices the flowers turning toward the child like faces. Emotional beat: quiet longing for purpose finally given a shape.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The guild archives reveal the child speaks the First Tongue, and fragments of her babble describe a king 'wearing something that wears him.' Elder Sefu orders the child confined; Lior secretly teaches her garden-words and learns her name: Iri. Emotional beat: first bond, first act of disobedience.

chapters.title: What the Ward Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Iri's POV, rendered in strange, sensory prose. Through her eyes we see the valley's magic-dead silence as a wound, and feel distant magic pulling at her like tide. She dreams of the king drowning inside his own crown. Emotional beat: dread establishing stakes beyond the valley walls.

chapters.title: The Guild's Quiet Lie
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior discovers the valley ward wasn't built to protect the world from magic — it was built to hide the guild's founding crime: they bound the First Tongue into the soil generations ago, and Lior was born of that binding. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty begins to crack.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Lior and Iri flee at night with Sefu's hunters behind them, crossing the ward line into a world where every sound carries weight and Lior's hidden nature flickers visibly. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the unknown.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The land itself tests them: a bridge of singing roots demands a true name, a village of oath-bound farmers mistakes Iri for an omen. Lior bargains with a river using half-remembered guild rites, discovering their 'worthless' training is really ritual grammar. Emotional beat: competence earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the capital they find Aldric lucid but fading, the crown-thing — a parasite of bound oaths — ruling through his mouth. A courtier loyal to the man, not the crown, smuggles them in. Emotional beat: horror of seeing loyalty weaponized into possession.

chapters.title: Sefu at the Gate
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. The guild hunters arrive not to punish Lior but to reclaim Iri: Sefu believes returning her to the valley will re-tighten the failing ward. Iri, who trusts almost no one, must choose between the elders' promise of safety and Lior's dangerous truth. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against love.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. Before the assembled court, Lior sings the First Tongue — the language written into their bones — while Iri gives the king back his own name. The crown shatters; the backlash unmakes the valley ward forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice, self-recognition, the cost of truth fully paid.

chapters.title: When the Garden Sings Anew
chapters.summary: Split POV, resolution. The valley opens its gates; the guild must become stewards rather than jailers, with Sefu kneeling in apology. Lior, no longer bound to the soil, plants the first freely grown seed and teaches Iri — and the kingdom — the old words as a living tongue, not a chain. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, grief transmuted into growth.
